Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("24604384b0e748ada07923630b3d037489e696284a98c4409fb9b6763565571f", "2014d09c7ded74d89c885b5f11693865224116f1b25df9330e61fe528f419d73") or SHA1 in~ ("24604384b0e748ada07923630b3d037489e696284a98c4409fb9b6763565571f", "2014d09c7ded74d89c885b5f11693865224116f1b25df9330e61fe528f419d73") or MD5 in~ ("24604384b0e748ada07923630b3d037489e696284a98c4409fb9b6763565571f", "2014d09c7ded74d89c885b5f11693865224116f1b25df9330e61fe528f419d73")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("24604384b0e748ada07923630b3d037489e696284a98c4409fb9b6763565571f", "2014d09c7ded74d89c885b5f11693865224116f1b25df9330e61fe528f419d73") or SHA1 in~ ("24604384b0e748ada07923630b3d037489e696284a98c4409fb9b6763565571f", "2014d09c7ded74d89c885b5f11693865224116f1b25df9330e61fe528f419d73") or MD5 in~ ("24604384b0e748ada07923630b3d037489e696284a98c4409fb9b6763565571f", "2014d09c7ded74d89c885b5f11693865224116f1b25df9330e61fe528f419d73")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["24604384b0e748ada07923630b3d037489e696284a98c4409fb9b6763565571f", "2014d09c7ded74d89c885b5f11693865224116f1b25df9330e61fe528f419d73"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Cisco FMC CVE-2026-20079 auth bypass: pre-auth CGI callServerFunc / csm_processes session abuse · [LLM] Cisco FMC static/built-in service account authentication (CVE-2026-20316) · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Cisco FMC Zero-Day Actively Exploited, Static Credentials Could Expose Sensitive
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Cisco FMC RCE artifact: www user runs package_info.pl as root against /var/tmp/license.tmp
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Cisco FMC RCE artifact: www user runs package_info.pl as root against /var/tmp/license.tmp AIInstallation High
Hunts the exact Cisco-published indicator of compromise for CVE-2026-20079/CVE-2026-20316 exploitation on Secure Firewall Management Center: the web-server account (www) invoking sudo to run /usr/local/sf/bin/package_info.pl against the attacker-controllable file /var/tmp/license.tmp as root. Legitimate license processing never targets /var/tmp/license.tmp, making this a near-zero-FP post-exploitation signal. Rationale: Anchored on the exact IOC line Cisco tells customers to grep for ('cat /var/log/messages | grep license' -> package_info.pl /var/tmp/license.tmp), corroborated by VulnCheck which confirms /var/tmp/license.tmp is the arbitrary-file-write target in the RCE chain. Defender/Falcon/CloudWatch are empty because FMC is a Linux appliance with no such agents; telemetry only reaches SIEM via Syslog. Cross-checked against: • https://www.vulncheck.com/blog/cisco-fmc-auth-bypass-cve-2026-20079 • https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/csa/cisco-sa-fmc-static-cred-BET3Cjh.html • https://horizon3.ai/attack-research/vulnerabilities/cve-2026-20079/
ATT&CKT1190 T1068 T1548.003
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Cisco TAC-guided troubleshooting where an engineer manually stages a license file (would rarely use the /var/tmp/license.tmp path)
  • Security team reproducing the Cisco IOC-check command during hunt (creates a benign grep hit, not an actual sudo execution)
  • Backup/restore tooling copying appliance state that replays old /var/log/messages content into the SIEM
  • Automated FMC health scripts invoking package_info.pl against the real license under /var/sf/, not /var/tmp/license.tmp
Suppression filter
| where SyslogMessage !has "grep" and SyslogMessage !has "COMMAND=/bin/grep"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm the log is a live sudo execution (USER=root, COMMAND=package_info.pl /var/tmp/license.tmp), not a benign grep of the IOC-check command; note the FMC hostname, appliance version, and timestamp. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the FMC management interface from untrusted networks, snapshot /var/tmp/ and /var/log/messages for forensics, then apply the branch hot fix (7.0.9.1 / 7.2.11.1 / 7.4.7.1 / 7.6.5.1 / 7.7.12.1 / 10.0.1.1) and rotate all admin/API credentials. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot to httpd access logs for the CVE-2026-20079 CGI bypass requests (sajaxintf.cgi callServerFunc, csm_processes session), review any managed-firewall policy pushes since the event, and check for new local accounts or SSH keys.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SyslogMessage has "package_info.pl" and SyslogMessage has "/var/tmp/license.tmp"
| where SyslogMessage has "USER=root"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, HostIP, Facility, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

Cisco FMC CVE-2026-20079 auth bypass: pre-auth CGI callServerFunc / csm_processes session abuse AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the CVE-2026-20079 authentication-bypass request chain against Secure FMC's web interface: unauthenticated calls to sajaxintf.cgi with rs=callServerFunc invoking validateLicense/batchResults/upgradeReadinessCall, and info-disclosure requests to about.cgi / ApplianceInformation.cgi riding the built-in csm_processes machine session. These endpoint+parameter combinations are the documented exploit primitives, not normal admin browsing. Rationale: Uses the exact CGI endpoints, query parameter (rs=callServerFunc), abused functions (validateLicense/batchResults/upgradeReadinessCall) and the csm_processes machine-session identifier that VulnCheck and Horizon3 document as the CVE-2026-20079 bypass-to-RCE primitives - none of which appear in normal authenticated FMC UI traffic. Cross-checked against: • https://www.vulncheck.com/blog/cisco-fmc-auth-bypass-cve-2026-20079 • https://horizon3.ai/attack-research/vulnerabilities/cve-2026-20079/ • https://kudelskisecurity.com/research/cisco-secure-firewall-management-center-fmc-authentication-bypass-and-rce-vulnerabilities
ATT&CKT1190 T1078.001
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorized vulnerability scanners (Tenable/Qualls/Horizon3 NodeZero) probing the FMC with the public PoC
  • Cisco TAC or internal red team validating patch status against these CGIs
  • Legitimate license/smart-licensing sync traffic that also touches validateLicense but from an authenticated admin session
  • Post-patch appliances still logging historical exploit attempts replayed from archived syslog
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify the source IP of the CGI requests and whether the FMC was rebooted recently (CVE-2026-20079 requires a persisted csm_processes session post-boot); confirm the appliance is on a pre-fix version. Step 2 (contain): Restrict the FMC management interface to trusted admin subnets, block the source IP at the perimeter, and apply the branch hot fix immediately (no workaround exists). Step 3 (hunt): Correlate with UC1 (www->root package_info.pl / /var/tmp/license.tmp) on the same host and timeframe to confirm bypass-to-RCE, then audit managed-firewall policy changes and new sessions in sfsnort.sessions.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (SyslogMessage has "sajaxintf.cgi" and SyslogMessage has "callServerFunc" and SyslogMessage has_any ("validateLicense","batchResults","upgradeReadinessCall"))
      or (SyslogMessage has_any ("/help/about.cgi","/platinum/ApplianceInformation.cgi") and SyslogMessage has "csm_processes")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

Cisco FMC static/built-in service account authentication (CVE-2026-20316) AIExploitation Low
Hunts logins to Secure FMC using the hard-coded/service accounts tied to CVE-2026-20316's static-credential weakness (report, sftop10user, SRU, Sourcefire, csm_processes). These accounts are internal service identities that should never interactively authenticate from a network source; a successful login is a strong indicator the static credentials are being abused for data access. Rationale: CVE-2026-20316 is defined by static credentials for a low-privileged account; VulnCheck enumerates the built-in FMC service accounts (report:snortrules, sftop10user, SRU, Sourcefire, csm_processes:csmdaemon) that ship with hard-coded passwords, so authentication as any of these from a network source is the article-specific abuse signal. Cross-checked against: • https://www.vulncheck.com/blog/cisco-fmc-auth-bypass-cve-2026-20079 • https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/csa/cisco-sa-fmc-static-cred-BET3Cjh.html • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisco-warns-of-fmc-static-credential-flaw-exploited-in-zero-day-attacks/
ATT&CKT1078.001 T1190
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal FMC daemons (csm_processes/csmdaemon) opening local sessions as part of normal snort/CSM processing
  • Cisco health-monitoring or reporting subsystems using the report/sftop10user accounts for scheduled queries
  • Log lines mentioning 'Sourcefire' as a product string rather than an account name (keyword collision)
  • Backup restore replaying historical auth events into the SIEM
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessName has "csm" and SyslogMessage has "session opened" and SyslogMessage !has "sshd")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Determine whether the login is a local daemon session or a remote/network authentication (source IP, SSH vs web); a network-sourced login as report/sftop10user/SRU/Sourcefire is high-suspicion. Step 2 (contain): Apply the branch hot fix (which removes/changes the static credentials), restrict the management interface to trusted networks, and rotate all appliance credentials and API keys. Step 3 (hunt): Review what sensitive data the low-privilege account could reach (device configs, event data), correlate with UC1 and UC2 on the same host to detect privilege-escalation chaining, and export any accessed reports for scope assessment.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("Accepted", "session opened", "authentication succeeded", "login succeeded")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("report", "sftop10user", "SRU", "Sourcefire", "csm_processes")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| sort by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"

    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Actions on Objectives
—
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Recon tool reading K8s service-account token or /proc/self/environ inside a container
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Cloud instance metadata (IMDS 169.254.169.254) queried by a recon tool inside a workload · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Recon tool reading K8s service-account token or /proc/self/environ inside a container AIReconnaissance Medium
Hunts an interactive/recon binary (cat, curl, python, base64, xxd) reading the mounted Kubernetes service-account token path or /proc/self/environ inside a workload — the day-1 in-pod enumeration the article describes ('a pod reading /proc/self/environ, inspecting service-account tokens'). Distinguishes credential/environment harvesting from a normal application startup read. Rationale: Uses the article's literal strings '/proc/self/environ' and 'service-account tokens' (mounted at /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount) plus recon-tool binaries, so it fires on enumeration rather than a library's normal token read. Cross-checked the K8s SA-token-theft chain in Unit42 and TheHackerNews' breach coverage. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/openai-agent-used-exposed-credentials.html • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/modern-kubernetes-threats/ • https://aquilax.ai/blog/kubernetes-service-account-token-theft
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1613 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Init container or entrypoint script that cats the SA token for debugging
  • CI/CD job (e.g. Helm, kubectl-in-pod) echoing token path during setup
  • Observability agent reading /proc/<pid>/environ for process metadata enrichment
  • Developer running an interactive shell in a pod during troubleshooting
  • Security scanner/CIS-benchmark tool auditing token mounts
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("kubelet","containerd","dockerd") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("entrypoint","docker-entrypoint","helm"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the pod/node (DeviceName), the process lineage, and whether the reader is the workload's own app or an injected shell/tool; pull the full command line and parent. 2) Contain: if the reader is not the expected app, cordon the node, kill the pod, and rotate the pod's service-account token and any secrets it could reach. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same DeviceName for subsequent connections to 169.254.169.254 (IMDS), privileged pod creation in K8s audit, and outbound to pastebin/request-capture/file-sharing services indicating C2 staging.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("cat","head","tail","curl","wget","python","python3","sh","bash","dash","busybox","base64","xxd","strings")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount","/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount","/proc/self/environ")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("cat","head","tail","curl","wget","python","python3","sh","bash","busybox","base64","xxd","strings")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount","/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount","/proc/self/environ")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cloud instance metadata (IMDS 169.254.169.254) queried by a recon tool inside a workload AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts a container-side recon binary (curl, wget, python, busybox) connecting to the cloud metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254 / 169.254.170.2) — the article's 'queried cloud metadata' step used to harvest node IAM credentials. Filtering on the recon tool separates credential theft from legitimate cloud-SDK IMDS calls. Rationale: Anchors on the well-known IMDS IPs (169.254.169.254 for AWS/Azure/GCP, 169.254.170.2 for ECS) paired with recon binaries, matching the article's 'queried cloud metadata' credential-harvest step while excluding in-app SDK IMDS traffic. IMDS-to-IAM abuse corroborated by Unit42/SecureByDezign. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/modern-kubernetes-threats/ • https://www.securebydezign.com/articles/kubernetes-pod-escape-cloud-takeover.html
ATT&CKT1552.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • cloud-init / bootstrap scripts curling IMDS for instance identity or user-data
  • kube2iam / kiam / IRDS sidecars that proxy IMDS via curl-like helpers
  • Health-check scripts querying instance-id or region from metadata
  • aws-cli/gcloud shell wrappers invoked by legitimate automation
  • Debugging session where an engineer manually curls IMDS
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("cloud-init","user-data","kube2iam","instance-id","api-token"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the initiating process command line — did it hit the credentials path (/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ or /computeMetadata/v1/) and was IMDSv2 token flow used? Identify the host/pod and its IAM role. 2) Contain: revoke/rotate the node or pod IAM role credentials, and add a GuardDuty/SCP guardrail; if creds were retrieved, assume they are compromised and rotate. 3) Hunt: pivot to CloudTrail for AssumeRole/API calls made with those temporary credentials from a source IP outside the VPC (see UC4), and check for privileged pod creation on the same node.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteIP in ("169.254.169.254","169.254.170.2")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl","wget","python","python3","sh","bash","busybox","perl","ruby","nc","ncat")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("169.254.169.254","169.254.170.2")
| where NetworkDirection == "Outbound" or isempty(NetworkDirection)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol, Url
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |

    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:

            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'

      a known-admin-host watchlist

ENDPOINT

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Critical Rails Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Read Server Files via Image Uploads

The Hacker News
2026-07-29 11 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Ruby on Rails has released fixes for a critical Active Storage vulnerability that could let unauthenticated attackers read arbitrary files from application servers through crafted image uploads. Tracked as CVE-2026-66066 (CVSS score: 9.5), the flaw can expose the Rails process environment and secrets such as secret_key_base, the Rails master key, database passwords, cloud storage credentials,

Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Active Storage direct-upload + representation abuse (CVE-2026-66066 libvips file read) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] libvips 'matload' / MATLAB-HDF5 unsafe loader invocation on Rails host · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)

Active Storage direct-upload + representation abuse (CVE-2026-66066 libvips file read) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts an unauthenticated source hitting the Rails Active Storage direct-upload endpoint and then repeatedly forcing variant/representation rendering — the exact request sequence needed to trigger the libvips matload file-read chain. Article-specific because it anchors on the fixed Active Storage route names that are present by default even when the app never uses direct uploads. Rationale: Anchors on the fixed Active Storage routes (/rails/active_storage/direct_uploads and /representations/) that Rapid7 identifies as the required, default-present entry point; the upload-then-render sequence from one source is the CVE-2026-66066 trigger pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-kindarails2shell-cve-2026-66066-critical-arbitrary-file-read-and-possible-remote-code-execution-in-ruby-on-rails/ • https://github.com/rails/rails/security/advisories/GHSA-xr9x-r78c-5hrm
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate users uploading avatars/photos then viewing the generated thumbnail on the same page
  • Load/uptime testing tools that exercise upload endpoints
  • CDN or image-proxy warmers pre-fetching representation URLs
  • Mobile app clients that direct-upload and immediately request the variant
  • Security scanners (Nessus/Qualys) probing Active Storage routes
Suppression filter
| where UserAgent !has_any ("UptimeRobot","Pingdom","StatusCake","GoogleImageProxy")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full request timeline for the flagged CIp — confirm a POST to direct_uploads was followed by representation/blob GETs, and check whether any session cookie/Authorization was present (exploit is unauthenticated). 2) Contain: block the source IP at the WAF and put direct_uploads behind auth or set VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED on the host. 3) Hunt: on the app host, correlate to UC 'libvips MATLAB loader' and UC 'Rails secret-file read' within +/-120s; if confirmed, treat secret_key_base, master.key, DB creds and cloud keys as compromised and rotate.
AppServiceHTTPLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where CsUriStem has "/rails/active_storage/direct_uploads" or CsUriStem has "/rails/active_storage/representations" or CsUriStem has "/rails/active_storage/blobs"
| summarize Requests=count(),
            Uploads=countif(CsUriStem has "direct_uploads"),
            Reps=countif(CsUriStem has "representations"),
            Statuses=make_set(ScStatus),
            FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated)
            by CIp, UserAgent, CsHost
| where Uploads > 0 and Reps > 0   // upload a crafted blob then force variant rendering = the exploit sequence
| order by Requests desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count, values(Web.url) as urls, dc(eval(if(like(Web.url,"%direct_uploads%"),1,null()))) as uploads, dc(eval(if(like(Web.url,"%representations%"),1,null()))) as reps from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*/rails/active_storage/direct_uploads*" OR Web.url="*/rails/active_storage/representations*" OR Web.url="*/rails/active_storage/blobs*") by Web.src, Web.http_user_agent, Web.dest, Web.status | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where uploads>0 AND reps>0 | sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(Web.url) as urls, dc(eval(if(like(Web.url,"%direct_uploads%"),1,null()))) as uploads, dc(eval(if(like(Web.url,"%representations%"),1,null()))) as reps from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*/rails/active_storage/direct_uploads*" OR Web.url="*/rails/active_storage/representations*" OR Web.url="*/rails/active_storage/blobs*") by Web.src, Web.http_user_agent, Web.dest, Web.status | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where uploads>0 AND reps>0 | sort - count
libvips 'matload' / MATLAB-HDF5 unsafe loader invocation on Rails host AIExploitation Medium
Detects the libvips matload operation or a MATLAB/HDF5 (.mat) attachment being processed by an Active Storage worker — the untrusted libvips loader Rapid7 identified as the CVE-2026-66066 file-read primitive. Rare in production: legitimate web apps almost never process MATLAB files through image variants. Rationale: Uses the exact libvips operation ('matload') and MATLAB/matio format Rapid7 names as the CVE-2026-66066 file-read primitive, scoped to a Rails/Active Storage parent (ruby/puma) — a combination with near-zero legitimate occurrence in a web app. Cross-checked against: • https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-kindarails2shell-cve-2026-66066-critical-arbitrary-file-read-and-possible-remote-code-execution-in-ruby-on-rails/ • https://www.libvips.org/2022/05/28/What's-new-in-8.13.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1211
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Data-science/imaging platform that genuinely ingests MATLAB .mat files via libvips
  • A developer manually running vips on a .mat sample during troubleshooting
  • Batch image jobs that enumerate mixed file types including .mat archives
  • Antivirus/File-scanning tooling reading .mat files (parent would not be ruby/puma — already excluded)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("clamd","clamscan","freshclam") or AccountName in~ ("datascience","jupyter"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the parent is a Rails/Active Storage worker (ruby/puma/passenger) and capture the target path argument and the invoking user. 2) Contain: kill the worker, set VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED=1 (libvips >=8.13) or Vips.block_untrusted(true), and pull the app off the LB. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same DeviceName/host to the secret-file-read UC and to outbound connections from the ruby process; if secrets were reachable, rotate secret_key_base, master.key, DB and cloud storage credentials.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("vips","vipsthumbnail","vipsheader")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("matload","VipsForeignLoadMat",".mat","matio")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("ruby","puma","bundle","rails","unicorn","passenger")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("matload","VipsForeignLoadMat","matio")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("vips","ruby","puma","active_storage",".mat")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Rails Active Storage libvips MATLAB Loader Invocation (CVE-2026-66066)
id: 3d9a1c74-2e18-4a6b-9f0d-2c5b7e41a8f2
status: experimental
description: Detects invocation of the libvips 'matload' / MATLAB (.mat) HDF5 loader by an Active Storage image worker, the untrusted loader abused in CVE-2026-66066 for arbitrary file read.
references:
  - https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-kindarails2shell-cve-2026-66066-critical-arbitrary-file-read-and-possible-remote-code-execution-in-ruby-on-rails/
  - https://github.com/rails/rails/security/advisories/GHSA-xr9x-r78c-5hrm
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/08/01
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/vips'
      - '/vipsthumbnail'
      - '/vipsheader'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'matload'
      - 'VipsForeignLoadMat'
      - '.mat'
      - 'matio'
  condition: selection_img and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
  - Scientific/imaging apps that legitimately process MATLAB files via libvips
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:(*matload* OR *VipsForeignLoadMat* OR *matio* OR *".mat"*) (@process.name:(vips OR vipsthumbnail OR vipsheader OR ruby OR puma) OR @process.executable.path:*/vips*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/vips(thumbnail|header)?$/i
| CommandLine=/(matload|VipsForeignLoadMat|matio|\.mat)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count, values(Processes.process) as cmdline from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("vips","vipsthumbnail","vipsheader") AND (Processes.process="*matload*" OR Processes.process="*VipsForeignLoadMat*" OR Processes.process="*.mat*" OR Processes.process="*matio*")) by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(Processes.process) as cmdline from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("vips","vipsthumbnail","vipsheader") AND (Processes.process="*matload*" OR Processes.process="*VipsForeignLoadMat*" OR Processes.process="*.mat*" OR Processes.process="*matio*")) by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | sort - count
Rails worker reads secret files after Active Storage upload (CVE-2026-66066 payoff) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the Rails/libvips worker process reading sensitive secret files (config/master.key, config/credentials.yml.enc, config/database.yml, .env, /etc/passwd) — the arbitrary-file-read payoff of CVE-2026-66066. Scopes the reader to ruby/puma/vips so it fires on exploitation, not on ordinary app boot reading its own config. Rationale: Targets the exact secret files the Rails advisory tells operators to rotate (master.key, credentials.yml.enc, DB creds) being opened specifically by a libvips/Active Storage worker — the observable result of the arbitrary file read, not app-normal config loading (which is ruby, not vips, at boot). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/rails/rails/security/advisories/GHSA-xr9x-r78c-5hrm • https://socprime.com/blog/cve-2026-66066-critical-rails-flaw-exposes-server-files-via-image-uploads/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Rails app boot / rake tasks reading their own config/credentials via ruby (excluded by scoping to vips)
  • Deployment tooling (Capistrano/Kamal) templating config files
  • Backup agents snapshotting the app directory including /etc/passwd
  • Config-management (Ansible/Chef) reading .env during a run
  • A developer running rails console reading credentials interactively
Suppression filter
| where ProcessName !in~ ("cap","ansible","chef-client","restic","borg","tar")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the reader is a libvips/Active Storage worker (not ruby boot or a backup agent) and note which secret files were touched. 2) Contain: isolate the host, revoke the app's cloud-storage IAM keys, and set VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED. 3) Hunt: rotate every secret readable by the app process (secret_key_base, master.key, everything credentials.yml.enc decrypts, DB creds, S3/GCS/Azure keys, third-party tokens) — Rails warns the patch does NOT invalidate already-stolen secrets — and review those services for logins from the attacker IP.
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where ProcessName in~ ("ruby","puma","vips","bundle","passenger","unicorn") or SyslogMessage has_any ("vips","active_storage")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("config/master.key","credentials.yml.enc","config/database.yml","/etc/passwd","/.env")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Exposure: unpatched Rails/libvips vulnerable to CVE-2026-66066 AIWeaponization High
Surfaces hosts still exposed to CVE-2026-66066 so the SOC can drive patching to Rails 7.2.3.2 / 8.0.5.1 / 8.1.3.1 and libvips 8.13+. Concrete: pivots on the CVE id in vulnerability telemetry plus libvips versions below the fixed 8.13 line. Rationale: Uses the concrete CVE id (CVE-2026-66066) plus the fixed-version cutoffs stated in the advisory (Rails 7.2.3.2/8.0.5.1/8.1.3.1, libvips 8.13) to enumerate exposed hosts — a clean exposure hunt with no payload ambiguity. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/rails/rails/security/advisories/GHSA-xr9x-r78c-5hrm • https://www.linuxcompatible.org/story/rails-7232-8051-and-8131-active-storage-security-patch-targets-cve202666066
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.All_Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Host flagged by CVE id but Active Storage not configured for Vips (not actually exploitable)
  • App accepts no untrusted uploads (lower real risk despite the flag)
  • libvips present but the vulnerable matload operation not compiled into the build
  • TVM lag: version updated but scan not yet refreshed
Response runbook
1) Triage: for each flagged host confirm whether the Rails app uses Vips (load_defaults 7.0+) and accepts untrusted uploads — these narrow true exposure. 2) Contain: prioritize internet-facing hosts; apply the interim VIPS_BLOCK_UNTRUSTED env var or Vips.block_untrusted(true) until the gem/libvips upgrade lands. 3) Hunt: on any exposed host, run the web-endpoint, matload, and secret-file-read UCs over the last 30 days to check for prior exploitation before patching.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-66066"
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by DeviceName asc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time

| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Fluentd aggregator pod contacts EC2 IMDS (169.254.169.254) — CVE-2026-54680 credential theft AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the Fluentd aggregator (ruby/fluentd process, or a shell/curl it spawned) reaching the cloud instance metadata service at 169.254.169.254. Post-injection, @type exec is used to curl IMDS for the node's IAM role credentials, as demonstrated in the advisory's EKS 1.35 PoC. Rationale: 169.254.169.254 is the literal IMDS endpoint in the advisory's EKS PoC (curl http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/...). A Fluentd log aggregator process reaching link-local IMDS is not normal application behaviour and indicates node-role credential theft. Cross-checked against: • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/kube-logging/logging-operator/CVE-2026-54680/ • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mjqf-28ph-426h
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1609
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • AWS SDK/SDK-based Fluentd output plugins (e.g. S3/CloudWatch/Kinesis) that legitimately resolve IAM role creds via IMDS — verify the initiating process and command line
  • kubelet/aws-node/CNI on the node hitting IMDS (node-level, not pod-scoped)
  • IRSA-migrated clusters where an SDK still probes IMDS as a fallback
  • Monitoring/health agents co-located on the node querying instance-id
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("iam/security-credentials","/tmp/imds","instance-id") and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("sh","bash","curl","wget")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the initiating process is fluentd/ruby or a shell it spawned (not a native AWS output plugin's SDK call) and inspect the command line for /latest/meta-data or iam/security-credentials. 2) Contain: rotate the node IAM role / affected IRSA credentials, restart the aggregator pod, and block pod egress to 169.254.169.254 with a NetworkPolicy; enforce IMDSv2 hop-limit=1. 3) Hunt: search CloudTrail for the node role's AssumeRole/API usage from unexpected IPs and pivot to UC 'Fluentd spawns shell' and any external egress from the pod.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "169.254.169.254"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("ruby","fluentd","fluent","sh","bash","dash","curl","wget")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr == "169.254.169.254"
| where NetworkDirection == "Outbound" or isempty(NetworkDirection)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol, EventProduct
| order by TimeGenerated desc
